messages:
Elena: quick note  onboarding feedback: users hit inconsistent param names across snippets (prompt / prompt_text / input). I'm leaning to `input_text` as the canonical API field since it's explicit and reads well in examples. Thoughts?
Micah: `input_text` reads fine to me. Slight preference for `user_input` historically, but `input_text` avoids confusion with non-text payloads in the future (we can reserve `input_blob` for binary later).
Noah: ok with `input_text` if we do two things: 1) publish a clear glossary row mapping all legacy terms to the new canonical ID; 2) add a repo-wide docs linter rule to fail CI on deprecated names in code fences.
Priya: agree. I'll draft a tiny "terminology matrix" Google Sheet with columns: canonical_id, legacy_terms, consumer_note, migration_snippet. Will link it from the style guide.
Elena: nice. One more UX ask: for Console labels keep the short label "Prompt" but show help text: "API field: input_text (formerly prompt/prompt_text)" for one release. That keeps the UI simple but informs power users.
Micah: for SDKs we'll keep a compatibility shim for one release and add migration examples in JS/Python. Example to include in migration doc:
```js
// old
client.generate({ prompt: 'Summarize' })
// new
client.generate({ input_text: 'Summarize' })
```
```py
# old
client.generate(prompt_text='Summarize')
# new
client.generate(input_text='Summarize')
```
Noah: DocsBot, can you run a scoped grep over /docs/examples and /docs/snippets (code fences only) and open PRs for straightforward replacements? Also run snippet-tests so we don't break sample code.
DocsBot: queued: scanning targeted folders for deprecated param names in code fences, opening fix branches, and running snippet-tests. Will post PR links here.
Priya: action items recap: Priya  create terminology matrix + draft glossary row; Noah  add docs-mdcheck rule + CI snippet-tests; Micah  prepare SDK migration snippets and compatibility note; Elena  UI help text ticket and release-note blurb. We'll land fixes after CI is green and then add the glossary link to quickstarts. :thumbsup:
